headline: The Nasdaq closed at a record 27,477.31 on Monday even as the US 10 year Treasury yield settled near 5.31 percent, its highest since 2002, while Brazil's Ibovespa jumped 7.70 percent to its first close above 200,000 after Flavio Bolsonaro led the first round of the presidential vote.

summary.us: The S and P 500 rose 0.66 percent to 7,773.95 and the Nasdaq Composite gained 1.05 percent to a record 27,477.31, led by Nvidia at an all time high near 238 dollars after it lifted its buyback authorisation by 150 billion dollars to 235 billion. The bond market pulled the other way: September ISM services eased to 54.9 but its prices paid index rose to 74.0, the highest since July 2022, leaving the 10 year Treasury yield near 5.31 percent and the 30 year around 5.66 percent.
summary.india: The Nifty 50 rose 0.56 percent to 22,555.75 and the Sensex added 453.04 points to 72,362.74, ending an eight week losing run, with ITC up about 5 percent while HDFC Bank fell 2.27 percent and Avenue Supermarts dropped about 6 percent after a Citi sell rating. Foreign investors sold a net 4,699.10 crore rupees in the cash market against domestic institutions buying 5,181.60 crore, and the rupee held near 96.3 per dollar ahead of the Reserve Bank decision on 7 October, where SBI Research looks for a 25 basis point increase to 5.50 percent.
summary.global: Japan's Nikkei 225 led Asia near 70,174 after the ruling party elected Sanae Takaichi as leader, which traders read as reducing the odds of a Bank of Japan increase this month, while the Hang Seng added 0.28 percent, the FTSE 100 rose 0.34 percent and the DAX gained 0.09 percent. Brazil was the outlier: the Ibovespa rose 7.70 percent to 206,911.89 and the real strengthened about 4.6 percent to 4.9859 per dollar after Flavio Bolsonaro took 47.03 percent of valid votes against Lula's 45.16 percent, setting a runoff for 25 October.

weekly.narrative: The bond market set the terms for four days and then handed them back on Friday. The US 10 year Treasury yield touched about 5.23 percent intraday midweek, described in coverage as the highest since June 2007, which pushed the dollar index to fresh 2026 highs, sent gold about 3.5 percent lower on the week and left the Dow down 1.3 percent and the S and P 500 down 0.3 percent even after Friday's bounce. Friday's September payrolls print of 29,000 against about 90,000 expected, with unemployment at 4.2 percent, cut October Fed hike pricing to near 37 percent from roughly 70 percent earlier in the week, and the Nasdaq Composite rose 1.19 percent with Nvidia at an intraday record and Tesla up 4.65 percent on 486,532 third quarter deliveries. India had the worse week and the shorter one: the Nifty fell 2.78 percent to 22,421.95 by Thursday's close, within 0.4 percent of its 52 week low, on rate increase fears, 91 dollar crude and foreign selling of about 44,000 crore rupees in September, before markets shut on Friday for Gandhi Jayanti. Hong Kong reopened from its own holiday to its largest fall since March with HSBC down 5.7 percent, Tokyo slipped as September core CPI came in at 2.7 percent against 2.4 percent expected, and silver lost 5.5 percent while copper held near records on tight supply. Next week turns on the 7 October FOMC minutes and the Reserve Bank decision the same day, with TCS opening India's earnings season on 8 October and the Strait of Hormuz still the swing factor for oil.
